newsitem.title: UK: Insurance brokers to unveil world network in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Insurance brokers to unveil world network in Feb.

text.p: World Insurance Network (WIN), an industry-wide electronic communications system being developed by the world's six biggest insurance brokers, will be unveiled in February.

The service, under development since November last year, will be demonstrated at a conference -- 21st Century Business Technology for the London and International Insurance markets -- in London on February 19, WIN joint chief executive David Evans told Reuters in an interview.
WIN is currently being tested by its backers and testing will be extended to include five selected insurers early next year.

WIN should go live in the first half of 1997, Evans said, initially with a secure messaging and e-mail service and a global insurance directory for members over an intranet system called WinConnect. He added that the emphasis has been on producing a product that works rather than sticking to timetables.

"The industry has got to change and reduce its cost base...We're convinced that WIN is the route forward, not only to attack our cost base, but to fund new products and change the way we bring them to market," Evans said.

The initial backers are Alexander & Alexander, Aon Corp, Johnson & Higgins, Marsh & McLennan, Sedgwick Group Plc and Willis Corroon Group Plc. British Telecommunications and MCI are providing communications expertise.
